drills.title: A tiny function box
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines (and indent them with the arrow buttons) so the program prints the number of months in 2 years. Two lines do not belong.
drills.explain: A function body is indented under its def line. return hands the result back to whoever called the function, so print(emi_months(2)) can show it. The call comes after the definition.

drills.title: Pick the operator
drills.prompt: Fill in the operators and the number so the program prints the goal output.
drills.explain: // drops the decimals (7 // 2 is 3), % is the remainder (1), ** is the power (8). divmod(125, 60) returns (2, 5): 2 hours and 5 minutes.

drills.title: Numbers surprise
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: / always gives a decimal. round() sends .5 to the nearest even number (2 and 4). Decimals are stored in binary, so 0.1 + 0.2 is not exactly 0.3. ** goes before *, which goes before +.

drills.title: The power trap
drills.prompt: The area of the square should be 16, but the program prints something else. Click the faulty line and choose the fix.
drills.explain: ^ is not a power in Python: it is a different operation (bitwise XOR), so 4 ^ 2 gives 6 without any error. The power operator is **.

drills.title: Review the AI's delivery summary
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote this summary. It runs, but two things are wrong or fragile. Tick them.

issues.text: The total is printed without rounding, so it can show float noise like 70.76459999
issues.why: Money should be shown with two decimals, for example f"{total:.2f}" or round(total, 2).

issues.text: hours = minutes / 60 gives 2.0833..., not whole hours
issues.why: / always returns a float. For whole hours use minutes // 60 (or divmod(minutes, 60)).

non_issues.text: % is the wrong operator for the remainder
non_issues.why: % is exactly the remainder operator: 125 % 60 is 5.

non_issues.text: Multiplying a float by an int (price * qty) raises an error
non_issues.why: Python mixes int and float freely. The result is a float.

non_issues.text: gst is computed before subtotal exists
non_issues.why: subtotal is assigned on line 3, before gst uses it on line 4.

drills.explain: Generated code often does the maths right but shows or splits numbers badly. Always ask: is this the right division (/ vs //) and is a money value formatted for people?
